candidate.educational_objective: Teach the biphasic hormonal effect of leuprolide in prostate cancer: an initial transient testosterone rise followed by sustained suppression with continuous therapy, including awareness of early tumor flare.

options.A: Testosterone may rise briefly after treatment begins, then falls with continuous therapy as gonadotropin secretion is suppressed.
options.B: Testosterone falls immediately after the first injection because leuprolide directly blocks androgen receptors.
options.C: Testosterone remains unchanged because leuprolide works by directly destroying rapidly dividing prostate cells.
options.D: Testosterone rises throughout therapy because leuprolide continuously stimulates pituitary gonadotropin release.

candidate.rationale: Leuprolide is a GnRH agonist. Initial administration can increase LH and FSH and transiently raise testosterone; with continuous therapeutic administration, gonadotropin secretion is suppressed and testosterone subsequently falls to castrate concentrations. This initial testosterone rise can worsen prostate-cancer symptoms during the first few weeks, so the client should be monitored for tumor-flare manifestations. Leuprolide does not act by directly blocking androgen receptors or by nonspecific cytotoxic destruction of rapidly dividing cells.
candidate.source_claim_supported: LUPRON DEPOT initially increases gonadotropins and testosterone; continuous leuprolide administration suppresses gonadotropin secretion and lowers testosterone to castrate concentrations. The label warns that the initial testosterone rise can cause tumor flare and worsening prostate-cancer symptoms during the first weeks.
